title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — better rest in Calvin's Clavis: Hebrew 'sin' often quality/condition, not act
pass_a_gloss: Better, he says, to rest with Calvin and not slight the Clavis Scripturae on peccatum: Hebrew 'sinned' (Qal) often means an inherent quality or condition—being a sinner, being guilty—not a discrete action, just as Hebrew verbs often mark a thing's existence rather than motion.
pass_b_english: You would therefore, in my judgment, have done better if, resting in Calvin's interpretation, you had not despised what you could read in the Clavis Scripturae under the name peccatum. He writes that the verb "sinned" in the Qal conjugation often signifies not an action, but an inherent quality, or a man's lot and condition, or to be a sinner, to be guilty—just as Hebrew verbs very often indicate only the existence of a thing, not an action or passion or other motion.
source_text: Rectius igitur mea sententia fecisses, si Calvini interpretationi acquiescens non contempsisses id quod legere potuisti in Clavi Scripturae ad nomen peccatum, his verbis: significat quoque crebro verbum חטא peccavit in prima conjugatione non actionem, sed qualitatem inhaerentem, seu sortem ac conditionem hominis, seu esse peccatorem, esse reum, sicut solent verba hebraea saepissime tantum existentiam rei, non actionem aut passionem aliumve motum indicare.
